justification: One Python headline string used by the evidence page and the area check, plus one sentence on the evidence page; above minor because it changes a served string.

pre_impl.existing_data: none: the headline is built per request from the area decision, nothing stored
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If walk_low_m differs from walk_high_m (an old range answer) the original range wording is still printed, so older shapes are unchanged
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every new area-check response; cached responses keep the old headline until they expire

functions.name: _headline
functions.input: pathway string plus the lmr and tod result dicts
functions.output: headline string shown on the evidence page and the area-check card
functions.if_none: both figures None prints 'no walk figure is available' instead of 'None m' (tested)

break_it.scenario: low and high both None on the lmr pathway
break_it.what_happens: headline reads 'no walk figure is available', not 'None m'

break_it.scenario: an older range answer (low 900, high 1060) hits the same builder
break_it.what_happens: it must still print the range wording
break_it.how: the else branch keeps 'walking range lo-hi m'; test_unmapped_span_figures_and_detail_use_the_range_wording covers the detail text

break_it.scenario: the frontend card parses the headline text
break_it.what_happens: a card could lose its range display
break_it.how: area-check-card.test.tsx uses a fixed headline string and passes (190 evidence and area-check jest tests)

falsifiable_check.fails_when: the headline prints 'walking range N-N m' for a single measured walk
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Reverting the headline change makes test_a_single_measured_walk_is_worded_as_a_walk_not_a_range assert on 'range' in the string; with the change, 105 passed

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: open the Penrith evidence page after the Railway deploy and read 'How this was measured'
